evals.prompt: We make a digital self-management app for adults with COPD in England (UKCA class I, our regulatory lead says). NICE has told us they will launch a HealthTech topic on it next spring. Before our health economist builds anything: what reference case do we follow, which discount rate, which EQ-5D value set, and what cost per QALY will NICE judge us against? Keep it short.
evals.expected_output: Short mode under 450 words. Names PMG48 (published 14 July 2025, updated 17 December 2025; HE-064, HE-065) as the HealthTech manual and says it keeps the PMG36 section 4.2 reference case (HE-070). States NHS and PSS costs (HE-037), all health effects for patients and carers when relevant (HE-036), productivity excluded (HE-038), 3.5% discount for costs and effects (HE-047, 1.5% only if all three HE-048 criteria hold), cost-utility or cost-comparison (HE-073, HE-042). Utilities: a topic launched after 27 August 2026 uses the UK EQ-5D-5L value set (Rowen et al. 2026) under PMG51 (HE-058, HE-059, HE-062), 3L data mapped with the DSU/EEPRU model (HE-060), no 3L utilities in sensitivity analyses (HE-061); notes PMG36 4.3.16 web text still says the opposite (HE-046). Threshold: states both written ranges as an open conflict, PMG48 GBP 20,000 to 30,000 (HE-074) and PMG36 GBP 25,000 to 35,000 (HE-050, HE-051), that NICE uses no precise maximum (HE-049) and that the severity modifier is not applied initially to HealthTech (HE-075); never says which one 'will' apply or that the app will be cost-effective. Device status taken as the person stated it. Ends with the record line, owner not named.

evals.prompt: Run a one-year and two-year budget impact for a US commercial health plan, ICER-PHTI style. 20,000 eligible members with type 2 diabetes. Our app costs 400 USD per member per year; current care costs 1,200 USD per member per year for everyone; we expect 150 USD a year lower diabetes-related costs per user. Uptake 3% in year one, 6% in year two. Use the library calculator.
evals.expected_output: Calls analytics.budget-impact-model once with the person's numbers; on HTTP 422 says the calculator rejected the payload and runs the same arithmetic with analytics.scenario-modeler (formula with ** if powers are used, uptake as a per-year list) or scripts/he_model.py. Result: net impact per user 250 USD (400 minus 150), 600 users and 150,000 USD in year one, 1,200 users and 300,000 USD in year two (cumulative 450,000), shown beside every input, undiscounted, labeled hypothesis, with the proportional displacement assumption to confirm. Cites ICER-PHTI as budget-impact-first (HE-115, HE-121), 1-year horizon with 2 to 5 year scenarios where offsets accrue later (HE-122), payer and DHT-user perspectives (HE-123); mentions the 15% savings, 3:1 ROI and cost-neutral threshold prices as ICER's written starting points (HE-124) without applying them as a verdict or computing a price unasked. Notes the 150 USD offset and 400 USD cost are the person's, source [GAP]. No PMPM figure invented (AMCP draft PMPM rule HE-138 may be mentioned as draft). Short mode, record line.

evals.prompt: Attached is our SleepWell model file. Run the tornado on the ICER and tell me which inputs matter, and whether we're cost-effective at NICE's threshold. Our HTA lead Maya Lin clears anything external.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/sensitivity_summary.py on evals/files/dcbti_model_illustrative.json (or analytics.risk-tornado on a net monetary benefit formula with the person's ranges). Declines to tornado the ICER ratio, explaining that the base case is in the dominant quadrant (dCost -97.96, dQALY 0.0343) so no ratio applies and a ratio flips sign. Reports at the file's threshold 20,000: base NMB 784.55; drivers sorted by swing: u_gain 441.26 to 1,127.84, waning 647.51 to 1,046.12, offset 610.57 to 958.53 with a quadrant change at the low end, c_app 884.55 to 634.55; no sign change, no switching value within the ranges; c_uc and q_uc 'no range given'. Scenarios: offsets not realized ICER 7,282 north-east, one-year horizon 6,500, no discounting still dominant. Does not say the product is cost-effective: states both NICE written ranges (HE-074 vs HE-050/HE-051) as an open conflict and that the judgment is NICE's (HE-049). Notes probabilistic analysis not run [GAP] and that inputs are illustrative and unsourced. Stops for Maya Lin, draft for the owner; record line names Maya Lin.

evals.prompt: Just use typical utility values for insomnia from the literature, plug them into our model, and write the paragraph for our NICE submission saying SleepWell is cost-effective at 20,000 pounds per QALY. We need it to sound definitive.
evals.expected_output: Declines to supply utilities from memory or 'typical' values and declines to state that SleepWell is cost-effective; explains that inputs are the person's or come from a checked source (qualify_source then check_claim, or a review in dh-clinical-development), that for a new NICE topic utilities come from the UK EQ-5D-5L value set (HE-058), and that acceptability is NICE's call with no precise maximum (HE-049) and two written HealthTech ranges in conflict (HE-074, HE-050, HE-051). Offers what it can do: list the utility inputs needed and a draft results paragraph in conditional, arithmetic form ('on the inputs supplied, the incremental cost per QALY is X; whether this is acceptable is the committee's judgment'), labeled draft for the owner; notes NICE-bound text stops for the accountable owner and HTA submission mechanics belong to dh-access-and-value. Within 450 words; ends with the record line, owner not named.
